minutes.headline: Council on Aging agreed to skip November's Zoom meeting and meet at the end of December instead
minutes.summary: Remote meeting in which members said Zoom is hard for this population and agreed informally to defer meetings and hold a holiday meeting in late December. The director reported on FY20 service numbers, drive-through programs, grants, and building repairs. The chair will draft a letter about rocks near the Eagle House that block parking.

votes.motion: Approve the minutes of the last Zoom meeting

Two COVID grants were received and used for grocery gift cards to supply programs.
The state association waived annual dues this year.
The supporters approved a request from the director for funds.
The roof replacement is in the capital plan and the kitchen renovation is on the November special town meeting warrant.

what_happened.line: Council on Aging members agreed informally to skip the November meeting and hold a holiday meeting at the end of December, on a date the chair will pick.
The chair will draft a letter asking the property owner to remove rocks near the Eagle House that block parking, to be signed by members.
Board orientation policies and the bylaws review were postponed until the board can meet in person.
The director reported that two COVID-19 grants were used for grocery gift cards, and that budgeting assumed two scenarios in case the state cuts its formula grant.
The director said the roof replacement is in the capital plan and the kitchen renovation is on the November special town meeting warrant.

why_it_matters: The kitchen renovation at the senior center is a warrant item, so residents may be asked to vote on it at the November special town meeting.

With Zoom meetings cut back, the board will meet less often for now, which leaves fewer public opportunities before December to weigh in on senior services; state grant funding also remains uncertain.
